models: none (offline: SQLite FTS5 keyword search; no model calls)
notes: Arm: --tokenizer unicode61 (FTS5 tokenize='unicode61'; the shipped default is 'porter'). This receipt is one arm of a two-arm tokenizer comparison and must be read with its sibling: docs/benchmarks/results/cuad-retrieval-porter.json (the shipped arm) and docs/benchmarks/results/cuad-retrieval-unicode61.json (stemming off). The index tokenizer is the only variable: both arms chunk identically and score identically, and each recorded every query in the committed benchmark (4,042 queries over 462 contracts). The shipped choice was originally made on a 1,536-query comparison whose harness was never committed and whose query count matches no benchmark in the tree, so that evidence cannot be reproduced; this pair is the re-derivation on the committed set. It reproduces the same direction (porter ahead) but not the same magnitudes: porter is +0.0124 hit@1, +0.0658 hit@5 and +0.0273 MRR@5 here, against the remembered +1.7 / +2.1 / +1.9 percentage points. Measured by scripts/measure_retrieval_accuracy.py, which reuses the product chunker (stream_chunks(ChunkConfig()) over one Clause per blank-line paragraph) and the product ingest path (ingest_document, per-document SQLite FTS5 index) but cannot reuse the product parser, which reads PDF/DOCX only and not the CUAD .txt corpus; chunk boundaries therefore approximate a real product parse. Ground truth is character-span overlap between a retrieved chunk and the query's CUAD answer span, not answer correctness, so a chunk that merely touches an answer span counts as relevant - this is the weakest link and it is why the absolute hit@1 is low. Retrieval depth is 20, deeper than the product default top_k of 5, so hit@5/MRR@5 are not an artifact of the cut. The receipt is the raw script output plus this metadata block (command/date/git_commit/models/provenance/notes), matching the other receipts here; wall time is machine-dependent. The corpus and the benchmark are gitignored (data/legalbenchrag/) and not redistributed. This measures retrieval, not query answering: nothing here checks whether an extracted answer is right. Recorded commit is the rebased twin of 8bd72a3 (identical tree): the branch landed on main by rebase, which rewrote every commit hash, so the original hash is no longer in main's history; the measured content is byte-identical.
chunking_rule: one chunk per blank-line-separated paragraph via openreview_cli.chunking.stream_chunks(ChunkConfig()) (chunk_size=512 tokens, chunk_overlap=50, group_short_clauses=True); paragraphs longer than 512 tokens are split by the product splitter. Offsets are document-global, translated through each clause's source_span.
ground_truth_rule: a chunk is relevant if its document character span [char_start, char_end) overlaps the query's CUAD answer span [start, end): char_start < end and char_end > start
caveats: Ground truth is character-span overlap, not semantic answer correctness; a chunk that merely touches an answer span counts as relevant. This is the weakest link.

The product parses PDF/DOCX only; the CUAD .txt corpus is chunked by building paragraph-level Clause objects and driving the product chunker directly, so chunk boundaries approximate -- but do not equal -- a real product parse.
Each contract is indexed alone and its index reused across its queries, matching the product's per-document index; there is no cross-document retrieval.
hit@1/hit@5/MRR@5 are macro-averages over queries (each query weighs equally).
Equal BM25 scores are ordered by SQLite without a stable tiebreak.
